title: Muse Wonder
author: meetpateltech
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Researchers introduce Muse Wonder and discuss its capabilities. playback position0:00 of 0:00 A frontier model that leads on personal and professional agents Today, we’re excited to introduce the Muse Wonder series with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, our most capable models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on personal and professional agentic tasks. Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence. Muse Wonder brings together Active Memory and Active Focus to keep track of what matters to you and work diligently toward what you want to accomplish. Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, and Muse Wonder Full is available today for Muse Code subscribers. Muse Wonder will soon power experiences in Muse, and will roll out first to subscribers. Muse Wonder will also power artifact generation and processes that require more intelligence. And in the future, we’ll be using Muse Wonder to develop specialized models that we can bring to everyone using Muse.Scaling Toward Personal Superintelligence Fourteen months ago, we began a ground-up overhaul of our artificial intelligence efforts. In that time, we’ve gone from rebuilding our stack from first principles to pushing the frontier.

When we introduced Muse Spark, we outlined our approach to predictable, rigorous scaling. Today’s release builds on that work across pretraining and reinforcement learning, delivering our most capable models yet. Trained at our gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full bring together the work of teams across Meta to deliver frontier capabilities for complex tasks at work and in everyday life — another step toward bringing personal superintelligence to the billions of people who use our products. Frontier Capabilities Model Highlights The Muse Wonder series achieves state-of-the-art results across key benchmarks for personal and professional agents, memory, and coding.
The full results below compare Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full with other frontier models across a broad evaluation suite.

For more details about our evaluations, see our report. The results above provide a broad view of the models’ performance. We now take a closer look at four areas central to their work on real-world tasks: domain expertise, Active Memory, Active Focus, and frontier coding. Domain Expertise Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full apply specialized knowledge to problems people encounter at work and in daily life, from understanding a lease to making sense of financial or health information. Our evaluations include tasks in law, finance, and health that test this ability. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), for example, requires models to work with source documents and follow detailed instructions to produce legal work products.

Active Memory One of the most critical steps towards useful personal and professional agents is reliable memory. Models need to remember what matters and recognize when earlier information becomes relevant. We call this Active Memory: carrying important context about you across conversations and actively retrieving the details relevant to the task at hand.

comments.author: atleastoptimal
comments.textRawHtml:
I personally have many problems with Meta, but imo the more companies close to the frontier, the better.

If only one company were calling all the shots once they hit recursive self-improvement, it would lead to extreme concentration of power, and their values being enforced across the entire industry. With 3-4 companies at the frontier, there is more urge to cooperate to avoid a catastrophic race condition.

children.author: fwipsy
children.textRawHtml:
That's not how nuclear arms control works, in most cases. Saying it's how superintelligence would work is a strong assertion. Especially since a true aligned superintelligence would make it much easier to finesse/manipulate the situation in your favor in nonviolent ways.

Not saying I think countries should be trying to win, but I don't think this win condition is impossible.

children.author: GodelNumbering
children.textRawHtml: All proponents of RSI seem to massively underestimate the problem of verification. Verifying that a hypothetical version N+1 is better than version N is an extremely hard problem. Especially so because you only have two possible verifiers - humans and the version N - both of which are out of their depth wrt N+1's capabilities. Not saying this is impossible, just that it is hard and slows things down.

children.author: breuleux
children.textRawHtml:
It's also unclear how intelligence actually scales in practice. A greater intelligence would be better at researching intelligence, but also harder to improve, so why would it explode rather than go up steadily? What are the actual resource requirements of various types of intelligence like persuasion or embodied intelligence? Coding, translating, copywriting, could very well be low-hanging fruits, very easy tasks we're very bad at, which doesn't say much about the hard tasks we're good at (embodied/animal intelligence, most likely).

There is also the problem of alignment, which is verifying that version N+1 behaves in a way that version N approves of. This is ostensibly the problem that we humans have with respect to AI development -- how to make sure they align with our values -- but it's also true of AI with respect to its own successors. Improving oneself without losing the plot would necessarily be slower than throwing stuff at the wall like evolution does.

children.author: tibbar
children.textRawHtml: This is not necessarily true. One easy way to compare version N and N+1 is "how much work (test time compute) does N+1 need to do to match the previous capabilities of N". It is true that some domains are currently hard to verify (e.g. biology is more difficult than math), but this is less of an N vs N+1 issue and more of a data domain issue.

children.textRawHtml: How would you be able to know that N+1 hasn’t scraped a source containing the questions asked of N1 and optimized its answers ahead of time? In many ways that would be the logical course of action when you’re tasked with creating an LLM that is assessed by criteria X/Y/Z.

children.author: tibbar
children.textRawHtml: This is not an intelligence problem. It is in part an operational problem (have you properly set up the test), but it is mostly an alignment problem. Is the model cheating or not. Alignment is, indeed, very difficult.
